Commentary.Commentary: So far so good for the Saffas. They whitewashed the visiting side in the Test series and took the ODIs 3-2 in the decider. That should give them plenty of confidence, especially after testing out a few players. Pakistan did well in the 50-over format, as they really pushed South Africa till the final game, but just fell short. They would like to finish this tour on a high though. The T20I leg is up next and the first of the 3-match series takes place at 1800 local (1600 GMT) at this same venue. Do join in for that. Cheers!

South Africa captain, Faf du Plessis, is extremely happy with the performance from his team in the decider and states that it's their best performance of the series. Reckons that the ball was coming on a bit slower in the first six overs, but the way de Kock played just eased the pressure off the rest of the batsmen. Adds that him and van der Dussen got a chance to test themselves as well which he's pleased about. Continues saying that there's more clarity about what their best combination could be so is happy with the direction in which they're going. Credits Pakistan for playing excellent white-ball cricket but is happy with how his team responded in this final game. Ends by thanking the Newlands crowd for coming out and supporting the team like they always do.

Man of the Series, Imam-ul-Haq, says he had a point to prove when he came here, he did that so wants to thank the management and the skipper for his success. Thanks his parents as well for all their support. Feels that they had a tough Test series against South Africa, so it felt more comfortable to switch to the 50-over format. States that Grant Flower worked hard with him in the nets, which helped him perform well.

Man of the Match, Quinton de Kock, says the wicket played better in the second innings so he was able to play his shots more freely. Reckons that when he got out off the no ball, he just tried not to get too worried and focus on his usual game, which helped. Mentions that Pakistan have a tough bowling unit and they were always wary of the threat they possess.

Pakistan captain, Shoaib Malik, says they played well in the previous game but this time it didn't click. Adds that their top order, especially Babar Azam and Fakhar Zaman, couldn't capitalize on the starts they got. Mentions that if you get starts you have to convert, otherwise you lose. Continues saying that they will learn from their mistakes and try to improve themselves. On Imam-ul-Haq, Malik states that he's developing steadily and he's pleased to see that. On Shaheen Afridi now, the stand-in skipper says he's a talent who's coming along well too. Applauds Quinton de Kock for the kind of knock he played and stresses that he took the game away from them.

Pakistan looked a completely different team from the 4th ODI. The ruthless, clinical outfit was tamed and devoid of any spark or invention in this series decider. Barring Zaman (who got a life) and his 70 and Wasim's late cameo, there wasn't anything of mention for the touring team. Even with the ball, they just never seemed to get going. De Kock's early onslaught didn't help their cause either. Plenty to work on for them later. The presentation will be coming up shortly.

Signed, sealed and delivered. South Africa dominated this game from start to finish and came out victorious, rightfully. They started off well with the ball, limiting Pakistan to a mere 240 on a good batting deck courtesy a collective bowling effort. And then, cruised home with the bat without any trouble. The Proteas look a completely different side when de Kock is on form. He gave the perfect start and his eventual 58-ball 83 set the perfect platform. Du Plessis and van der Dussen then came in, took advantage of that platform and took the hosts across the finish line without any further hiccups, scoring their respective fifties in the process.

SIX! Finishes things off in style and gets to his fifty too. His 3rd in this series and ODI cricket. Well played, Rassie van der Dussen. He charges out to this floated delivery outside off and smokes it straight back down the ground for a flat maximum. SOUTH AFRICA WIN BY 7 WICKETS AND TAKE THE SERIES 3-2!
Driven through the covers for a couple of runs.
Too far outside off, Rassie can't get to it.
31st ODI fifty for Faf du Plessis! Another fine knock from the South African leader. Gets to the milestone by easing it down to long off for a single.
Landed short but it keeps low. Spins away and Faf defends it going deep inside his crease.
FOUR! Streaky runs. Tossed up well outside off, spinning away, du Plessis drives and it goes off the edge. Hafeez at short third man drives to his left but can't stop it from reaching the boundary.
Length ball on off, kept out from inside the crease on the off side.
Some chin music for the batsman, he lets that bouncer through to the wicket-keeper.
Full delivery aiming the base of off stump, a straight bat is brought down in defense.
Wrists this full delivery down the ground and takes off. Hasan Ali from mid on moves to his left, gets to the ball and fires a wayward throw. Single completed with ease.
Faf makes room, comes down the track to whack this away but seeing the extra bounce backs out of the shot.
Behind a length, quite close to off, kept out from inside the crease.
Flighted delivery on off, van der Dussen blocks it well. Only 14 needed for the hosts to win the series.
Full on middle, the skipper drives it through mid on for a single.
Full on off, van der Dussen drives it towards mid off for a single.
SIX! What a shot. Flighted delivery on middle, van der Dussen dances down the track and lofts it straight over the bowler's head for a biggie.
Flighted delivery on off, the batsman keeps it out.
Floated on off, van der Dussen defends off the front foot.
On a good length on off, du Plessis keeps it out.
Short of a length delivery, the batsman pulls it towards fine leg for a single.
Full on middle, van der Dussen flicks it to short mid-wicket. The fielder does well to stop it.
On off, van der Dussen defends off the front foot.
Short of a length delivery, du Plessis pulls it towards square leg for a single.
Length delivery on middle, van der Dussen tucks it towards the leg side for a single.
Shaheen Afridi comes back on.
FOUR! Good use of the feet from Faf du Plessis. Dances down, gets close to the pitch and hammers it straight back down the ground for a boundary. Just 25 needed in 84.
Shifts his weight on the back foot and crunches it to sweeper cover. Single to the total.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Darts it quicker, around off, van der Dussen stays back and keeps it out.
Short and outside off, some room on offer, Rassie cuts but can't beat point.
Lands it around off, on a driving length, van der Dussen prods forward and defends.
Bowls a bouncer, the skipper does well to duck under it.
On off, du Plessis taps it to short third man and goes for the single. The fielder there goes for the direct hit at the keeper's end but misses it. The skipper survives.
Good length delivery on off, the skipper plays it to point.
Length delivery on off, du Plessis blocks it well.
Good length delivery on off, the skipper keeps it out.
Length delivery on off, van der Dussen taps it towards point where Shadab puts a dive and does well to stop it. The batsmen take a quick run.
Flighted delivery on off, van der Dussen taps it towards point for a single.
Full on middle, du Plessis comes down the track and hits it towards mid on for a single.
Floated on off, the skipper defends off the front foot.
Tossed up on off, du Plessis drives it uppishly through covers. It is safe of the fielder at covers. The batsmen pick up a couple.
Skates down the track to this loopy ball and defends it back down the track.
Loopy leg break outside off, turning away, Faf defends it off the outer half towards short third man.
Shadab Khan back into the attack.
Shortish delivery pounded in, the South African captain stands tall and blocks it down beside him. A single is collected.
Back of a length into the body, worked away on the leg side for one run.
Beaten again! Length ball around off, Rassie hangs his bat inside the line and gets beaten.
Bouncer angling in on middle and leg, du Plessis swivels and pulls it with control along the turf through backward square leg. Single taken.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Length delivery just outside off, from around the wicket, holds its line and beats the outside edge as van der Dussen pokes at it.
Short delivery, the batsman cuts it towards point for a single. Big over for South Africa. 10 runs came off it. The hosts need 39 runs in 108 balls.
Floated on off, van der Dussen plays it to point.
Short on off, the skipper cuts it towards point for a single.
Short on off, van der Dussen cuts it towards point for a single.
SIX! Amazing shot. 50-run partnership between du Plessis and van der Dussen. Flighted delivery on middle, van der Dussen comes down the track and lofts it over long on for a biggie.
Full on middle and leg, du Plessis drives it past the bowler towards mid on for a single.
Drinks are on the field.
Closes the face, works it past the man positioned in front of square leg and both batsmen cross over.
Short of a good length, Amir makes it angle back in, Faf attempts to turn it on the leg side but is caught on the thigh pads.
Spears in a yorker, on the stumps, drilled straight to the man at mid on.
Wide! Short and down the leg side, easy call for the umpire to make.
Yorker fired in on middle and off, dug out well by bringing down a straight blade in response.
Accurate bumper on middle and off, the Protea skipper crouches low and evades.

Angling in on middle and leg from around the wicket, du Plessis nudges it behind square leg and takes off. Calls for the second instantly and rushes back. Completes the run cleanly too, beating the throw at the keeper's end. Good running.
Mohammad Amir returns.
Sprays it on the pads, flicked down towards fine leg for a couple of runs.
Skidding off the deck outside off, the flipper from Shadab, too easy for Faf to find the gap in the cover area and take one.
Down the track to this one and smacks it past his skipper towards long on. Jogs across to the other end and completes the single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Rassie comes ahead seeing the flight and dead-bats it.
Quicker through the air, outside off, Faf drives through the line and hits it through the cover region. One run to the total.
Wide! Floated down the leg side, van der Dussen tries to flick but misses and so does the keeper as it goes off his pads. It runs down as the batsmen take three. Wide signalled by the umpire as well.
Eases this through the big gap in the covers for one more. 8 runs off the over without a boundary.
The batsman has driven it through mid on. One run added to the total.
Rassie comes ahead to this one with a big stride and plays it to long off. Gets off strike with a run.
More flight on this, outside off, du Plessis with those strong wrists of his plays a whippy-drive through the covers for a single.
Provides some air on this, seeing the flight Faf charges out and drives it through the covers. Two more runs collected.
Flighted leg spinner on middle stump, Faf premeditates the paddle sweep and places it fine down the leg side. Gets a couple of runs for his effort.
Uses his feet again and pushes it to long on for a single. South Africa are cruising along here. Just 70 runs needed in 132 balls.
Tossed up delivery on middle and off, du Plessis steps out to get close to the pitch and defends.
Full and straight from Imad, it's pushed back to the bowler.
Full and fast on off, not much room to turn, du Plessis drives but can't beat Babar's dive at covers. Pakistan need something inspirational from somewhere.
Slower through the air, in line of the stumps, Faf stays right behind the line and blocks it well.
Darted flat outside off, cracked through the gap in the covers for one run.
Takes a big stride forward and eases the drive through mid off. One run to end the over.
Loopy and full, outside off, van der Dussen comes forward, gets close to the pitch and defends.
Gives this some pace, the leg break around off, van der Dussen cuts it with the turn and places it through cover-point. Two to the total.
Tossed up, du Plessis clears his front leg and finds long off with the drive. Gets a single for doing so.
Drifting in at first but then turning away, on off, Faf is watchful as he camps back and pushes it on the off side.
Quicker, flatter and shorter outside off, Rassie punches it off the back foot past point for a run.
Shadab Khan is back. Last roll of the dice from Shoaib Malik.
Faf du Plessis has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Van der Dussen smacks this flatter ball towards sweeper cover and rotates strike.
Goes against the turn and works it through square leg. Single taken.
Spinning away from around off, shorter in length, dabbed square on the off side.
Fraction straight in line, van der Dussen turns it in front of square leg for a single.
Darts it a bit quicker, on middle and leg, kept out from inside the crease.
Sweetly timed. Rassie van der Dussen places the drive through the covers. It won't go all the way, but it's enough to fetch him three good runs.
Too full and too straight, worked wide of short mid-wicket, towards mid on, for a double.
Angles it in again, but it's still too far outside off, pushed to the covers by the batsman. Wants the single but then decides against it.
Shortish delivery around off, from around the wicket, van der Dussen rises on his toes and taps it down in front of covers.
Good length delivery around off, another defensive shot on offer.
Angling into the batsman, on middle and leg, Rassie clips it off the pads but straight to the fielder.
Shaheen Afridi back on.
Leans into the full ball and knocks it to long on to keep strike.
Loopy and full on middle and leg, van der Dussen is well forward in defense.
Sticks on the back foot on this occasion and finds sweeper cover with a firm punch. Another run collected.
Quite slow again, turning away from off stump, du Plessis comes half-forward and defends.
Tossed up outside off, van der Dussen reaches out and drives it off the front foot to covers. Takes a quick single and completes it with ease.
Slower through the air, on middle and leg, du Plessis turns it to the vacant square leg area and crosses over.
Shortish delivery pounded in, close to off, blocked down on the off side by rising on his toes.

Hit well and hit straight, but too straight. Rassie van der Dussen drives it off the middle and hits the stumps at the other end. Faf, just in case, dives back in his crease. Didn't want to take any risks.
Speared in full, driven straight to the man at mid off.
Angling in at first but then straightens up a shade, Faf closes the face early and gets a safe leading edge to covers. Single to the total.
Play and a miss! Length delivery in the channel outside off, du Plessis loosely plays at it and misses.
Wide! Banged in short and it's angling way down, wide signalled by the umpire.
Back of a length delivery angling in from around off, Faf forces the punch to the man at cover.
On the shorter side, outside off, punched to long off for a single.
Full and darted around off, eased down to long off for one.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Sliding in on off stump, the batter gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Short and flat outside off, punched off the back foot through to sweeper cover.
Short and flat outside off, punched off the back foot into the off side.
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, Rassie plays inside the line and is beaten.
On middle and leg, worked to the leg side for a single.
Whoof! That kicked off. A short ball outside off, du Plessis looks to defend but suddenly, the ball shoots up and hits him on the glove. Does not show any pain.
Rassie van der Dussen walks in at number 5, replacing de Kock.

OUT! That is a stunning catch! No century for Quinton de Kock. Ahh.... the crowd is dejected, not disappointed. But in terms of the match, guess he has almost sealed the deal for the Proteas. A length ball, around middle and leg, Quinton tries to whip it across the line on the leg side. He gets more height than distance but for a second, it seems like it will clear the infield. But it was not to be so. Substitute Hasan Ali races across the turf, that too backwards, from short mid-wicket. He keeps his eyes on the ball and maintains his pace too. In the end, he gets there in perfect time and takes the catch with ease. Or makes it look easy. End of a stunning 58-ball 83 from QdK. 95 more needed from 178 balls. Surely no choking from here?
On a length around middle, worked through mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! Beautiful shot to end the over! Into the 80s swims de Kock. Full and outside off, thrown up wide, QdK reaches out and lofts it with finesse over cover for a boundary! 96 more needed now, from 180 balls.
Full and outside off, eased through the covers for a run.
Down the leg side, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.

Brings out the reverse sweep a month in advance and Imad fires it outside leg. But the unperturbed keeper-batsman goes through with his shot and gets it behind point for a run. The stand moves to 40 from 29 balls.
A touch short, punched wide of cover for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.

TOP EDGE, SIX! De Kock continues to make merry. 78 from just 55 balls, with 10 fours and 3 sixes already! A short ball, around middle and leg, Quinton goes for the hook but is done in by the pace. The delivery takes the top edge and flies over fine leg! Second six of the over, 18 runs from it!
FOUR! Hammered away! Short delivery, de Kock pulls it powerfully through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Outside off, du Plessis waits for the ball to come to him and steers it late towards third man for a run.
Played to the point region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Good length delivery on off, the keeper-batsman defends off the front foot.
SIX! Good shot. Short of a length delivery, de Kock pulls it over square leg for a biggie. Quinton de Kock is looking dangerous out here.
Short on off, the keeper-batsman cuts it towards point for a single.
FOUR! Good shot from Quinton. Too full on middle and leg, de Kock comes down the track and flicks it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Full on off, de Kock plays it to covers.
Full on middle and leg, the skipper drives it towards mid on for a single.
Tossed up on off, de Kock cuts it towards point for a single.
Floated on off, turn on this one, de Kock looks to defend but gets beaten by the away turn on this one.
Good length delivery on off, the skipper defends off the back foot.
Bowls a bouncer, du Plessis does well to duck under it.
FOUR! Good shot. Short of a length delivery, du Plessis pulls it through square leg for a boundary.
Again on a length on middle, de Kock flicks it towards square leg for a single.
The clouds are coming over... 'It won't rain,' says Mike Haysman assuringly.
Length delivery on middle, du Plessis pushes it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Length delivery on off, du Plessis defends off the front foot.
FOUR! De Kock and reverse sweeps. Going hand in hand today. Full and outside leg, Quinton again reverse sweeps it through point and gets a boundary.
Floated on off, de Kock drives it to mid off.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
Tossed up on off, du Plessis defends off the front foot.
Outside off, Faf looks to drive but the ball goes off the inner half of the bat back to the bowler.

18TH ODI FIFTY FOR DE KOCK! He continues to thrive after the no ball reprieve. Full and around middle, worked towards mid-wicket for a single. Can he stay till the end and guide the Proteas to a series win?
Full delivery on middle and leg, de Kock pushes it towards mid on for a single.
Good length delivery outside off, de Kock looks to cut but gets beaten by the away movement on this one.
Faf du Plessis walks in at number 4, replacing Hendricks.

OUT! Hendricks has holed out! This is a bit of luck for Pakistan. Nothing happening and all of a sudden, a gift arrives. A short ball outside off, really wide, Hendricks opts for the cut shot. But it is the wrong choice. He has to reach out for it and it ends up being an upper cut. Does not have enough on it to clear the fence and Shaheen Afridi does not have to run much to his right at third man. Fortunate for Amir and Pakistan. 141 needed from 212 balls. Do they still have time for a comeback?
Good length delivery on middle, Hendricks looks to flick but gets a leading edge towards mid off. There was no fielder there and he was safe.
100 UP FOR SOUTH AFRICA! They are easing towards victory. 141 more needed now, from 214 balls. The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman.
FOUR! Poor delivery from Shadab Khan. Short delivery on leg, de Kock pounces on it and pulls it through square leg fielder for a boundary. The fielder had no chance there.
Flighted delivery on off, Hendricks drives it towards covers for a single.
SIX! Fine shot. Full on middle, Hendricks comes down the track and sends it sailing over long on!
Floated on off, Hendricks keeps it out.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Dropped short, pulled uppishly towards deep mid-wicket for one.
Short of a length delivery, Hendricks looks to pull but gets off the bottom part of the bat. It goes towards mid-wicket. The batsmen take a run.
Length delivery on off, Hendricks taps it to point.
A full toss, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and around off, Hendricks looks to flick but gets a bit of a leading edge towards point.
Short outside off, Hendricks cuts it through point. Imam-ul-Haq from cover puts in a dive to save the boundary and does well to stop it. The batsmen pick up a couple.
Outside off, pressed in front of point for a run.
Full and outside leg, another reverse sweep employed, this time behind point for a single.
FOUR! Risky shot from de Kock. Flighted delivery on off, de Kock again plays a reverse sweep but this time away from first slip. It goes towards third man for a boundary.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Tossed up on middle, de Kock plays a reverse sweep towards point. The batsmen take a single.
Short delivery, Hendricks pulls it through mid-wicket for a single.
Length delivery on middle, Hendricks flicks it towards leg side for a single.
Full and around middle, flicked straight to mid-wicket.
On a good length, around off, watchfully blocked out.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! Good length delivery on off, Hendricks looks to defend but gets an outside edge past first slip for a boundary.
Full and down the leg side, flicked towards fine leg for a single.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Floated on middle and leg, Hendricks looks to push but goes of the outer half of the bat. It goes towards square leg. The batsmen pick up a couple.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Short delivery, de Kock looks to cut but gets a bottom edge on this one.

FOUR! Just over! Full on middle, de Kock chips it over mid-wicket and just about clears the leaping fielder inside the circle. Runs coming thick and fast now. Quinton has moved to 32 from 27 balls with 5 fours and a six.
Tossed up on off, Hendricks drives it towards covers for a single.
Shadab Khan into the attack.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Cutting in from a good length, on leg, goes off de Kock's thigh pad down the leg side. A leg bye is taken.
Shaping away from around off, it's guided down to third man for a single.
Back of a length outside off, kept out from the back foot.
FOUR! Three in a row, two for Hendricks now. Behind a good length outside off, Reeza stays back and cracks it square through the off side. Finds the fence again.

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries for South Africa, brings up the 50 for them in style. Full and well outside off, Hendricks uses the angle going away from him and drives it through point. A boundary results.
FOUR! Once again on a length outside off, de Kock cuts it square through point brilliantly to the fence.
Back of a length, Quinton pulls it away to mid-wicket.
On middle and leg, Reeza flicks it away to mid-wicket and gets off the mark after 6 deliveries.
Length delivery on middle, Hendricks calmly defends it.
Full length delivery on middle and leg, Quinton flicks it away towards deep mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Full outside off, de Kock flicks it away to the fielder at mid on.
Lands it on a length outside off, Hendricks keeps it out to see off the over.
Length delivery on middle and off, Reeza pushes it towards mid on.
Good length delivery on off, Reeza confidently blocks it off his front foot.
On a length on off, Hendricks defends it.
Length delivery outside off, Reeza leaves it alone.
Back of a length on middle and off, de Kock punches it to deep point for a run.
Reeza Hendricks walks in at no.3.

OUT! Caught behind! Pakistan eventually get a breakthrough. It has taken them 6 overs but they have dismissed the mighty Hash. It is on a length and just in the channel outside off. Amla throws his bat at it and it is flat-footed. Hence, an outside edge is induced. Simple catch for Mohammad Rizwan and Pakistan have their first. Amla flops again. 202 more needed from 264 balls.
Back of a length outside off, Hashim punches the ball straight to the fielder at cover.
On middle and leg, Hashim flicks it towards mid-wicket and picks up a brace.
Full on middle and leg, Amla drives it to the fielder at mid on.
FOUR! This is brilliant from Amla. Full outside off, Amla lofts it over cover and the ball races away to the fence.
In the air but safe. Slightly slower this one. Bowled at 129.0 kph. Amla tries to drive but is early in his shot because of the change of pace. The ball falls just short of Shoaib Malik at mid off.
Length delivery on off, de Kock defends it to see off the over.
On middle and leg, flicked away to the fielder at mid-wicket.
FOUR! Wonderful from de Kock. Full length delivery on middle and leg, Quinton gets on his front foot and drives it superbly through mid on for a boundary.

Good length delivery outside off, Amla brilliantly cuts it towards backward point. Shaheen Afridi comes running from third man and puts in a dive to save the boundary. The batsmen pick up only a single.
On middle and leg, Hashim nudges it to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Length delivery outside off, Amla defends it off his front foot.
On a length at middle and leg, de Kock gets an inside edge and onto the pads.
Full on off, de Kock pushes it to the fielder at point.
WIDE! Good length delivery down the leg side. Quinton tries to flick but misses. The umpire signals this as wide.
FOUR! Full length delivery on middle and leg, de Kock perfectly times and places his flick through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Back of a length delivery outside off, de Kock defends it with soft hands. He looks for a single but Amla turns it down straight away.
Good length delivery outside off, Hashim guides it away to third man and gets a very comfortable single.
Length delivery on the fifth stump line. Amla tries to cut it square but misses it.
Outside off, pushed straight to point. 13 runs from the over, could have had a wicket as well.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
A length ball outside off, slapped over covers for a couple.

CAUGHT OFF A NO BALL! Oh dear... big big big big big mistake. Quinton de Kock gets a life. That might mean death for Pakistan. Everything so good about this delivery. Banged in short, hurrying onto the batsman as he went for the pull and got a top edge. Simple catch for Mohammad Hafeez at cover. But then, when the umpire refers it upstairs to check the legality of the delivery, replays show that the foot has landed outside the crease! Come back, QdK and make use of the Free Hit...

FOUR! But a good comeback from the bowler. He fires in a yorker outside off, de Kock walks into the shot and tries to dig it out. The ball swings in late, takes the inside edge but sneaks past the stumps to the fine leg fence!

SIX! 'Wow!' exclaims Pommie Mbangwa on air. Almost a payback for the one missed before. What a shot. A length ball, around middle and leg, de Kock swings it casually, actually with a bit of disdain. Kaboom. Right into the stands at mid-wicket. 226 more needed from 286 balls. The stand moves to 15 from 14 deliveries.
Short and wide outside off, de Kock slashes but misses. Opportunity missed, one guesses.
FOUR! Wonderful. Back of a length delivery outside off, Amla gets onto his back foot and wonderfully times his drive through point perfectly for a boundary. First boundary of the innings for Amla.
Length delivery outside off, punched to the fielder at cover by Hashim.
Full on off, hit straight to the fielder at mid off.
Good length delivery on off, Amla hits it straight to the fielder at point.
Full on middle and leg, de Kock pushes it to mid on and takes a quick single.
Length delivery on middle and leg, Hashim punches it to mid on and takes a run.

Starts with a length delivery outside leg. Amla tries to flick but misses. Rizwan behind the stumps does well and collects it diving to his left. There was a stifled appeal but the umpire turns it down and signals it as wide. Snicko confirms the umpire was right.
Full around off, Quinton drives it to the fielder at cover to finish off the over.
Good length delivery on off, de Kock drives it straight to the fielder at mid off.
Full outside off, Quinton drives it straight to the fielder at cover.
Back of a length on middle, Amla gets off the mark by flicking it towards square leg.
Fuller length delivery outside off, de Kock flicks it to mid-wicket for the first run of the inning.
Starts with a full length delivery on middle and leg, de Kock tries to flick it but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
We are back for the chase. Quinton de Kock and Hashim Amla to open the innings for South Africa. Usman Khan to bowl the first over.
